result:
**Rebuttal (Debater B)**

Debater A's set {1, p^(n-1), p^(n-1)(p-1)} depends on the trivial subgroup working. A asserts that H = 1 gives an almost commutative Terwilliger algebra because only the trivial character exists, but that does not show the algebra is almost commutative. A never checks the p′-part at all, even though it is one of the most natural subgroups of Aut(G). Since Aut(G) is cyclic of order p^(n-1)(p-1), it has exactly one subgroup of each divisor order, so the candidate subgroups are fixed by their orders. The problem says exactly three work. A's choice drops the p′-subgroup of order p-1 and keeps the trivial subgroup without justification. My set {p^(n-1), p-1, p^(n-1)(p-1)} keeps the two structurally distinguished subgroups, the Sylow p-part and the p′-part, together with the full group.

A's objection to my answer is that an order-p subgroup such as the one on Z_27 spreads its Gauss sum over several orbits. That is a claim about a different subgroup. The distinctness check also settles the arithmetic: since p ≥ 3 and n ≥ 2, the three orders are distinct, so the sum is p^n + p − 1.
